chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqah from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father (peace be upon him) that Ali (peace be upon him) said:

There is no one among the children of Adam except that his forelock is in the hand of an angel. If he becomes arrogant, the angel pulls him by his forelock to the earth and says to him, 'Be humble,' and Allah will humble you. And if he is humble, the angel pulls him by his forelock and then says to him, 'Raise your head,' and Allah will raise you and not humble you due to your humility for Allah.
ai.seo_question: How does humility affect a person's spiritual status according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* illustrates the metaphysical reality of *nasīyah* (forelock), a concept rooted in Surah Al-Alaq, where angels physically manifest divine response to human character. It emphasizes that humility is not merely a social virtue but a spiritual mechanism that elevates the believer, while arrogance invites immediate divine lowering, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on *tawāḍuʿ* as a path to nearness to Allah.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ali Majluwayh from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim from Harun b. Muslim from Mas’ada b. Sadaqah from Ja’far b. Muhammad from his father (a.s.) that Ali (a.s.) who said:
Keep your head up. There is a lot of honor for you near Allah and you won’t be disgraced due to your humility.”
